title: Boss: the resolver
summary: Simulate a resolver: follow CNAMEs, catch loops, and explain the path.

steps.title: Build a resolver
body: Every step uses a zone of `(Name, Type, Value)` records. Names compare case-insensitively. A resolver asked for type `A` on an alias follows the `CNAME` chain until it finds `A` records.

steps.title: Follow the chain
prompt: Write `List<string> Resolve(List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)> zone, string name, string type)`:
1. If `name` has records of `type`, return their values.
2. Else if it has a `CNAME`, continue with its target.
3. Else return an empty list (NXDOMAIN / no data).
If the chain visits a name twice, throw `InvalidOperationException` (a CNAME loop).
starter: List<string> Resolve(List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)> zone, string name, string type)
solution: List<string> Resolve(List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)> zone, string name, string type)
if (!seen.Add(current)) throw new InvalidOperationException("CNAME loop at " + current);
var direct = zone.Where(r => string.Equals(r.Name, current, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && r.Type == type)
var cname = zone.FirstOrDefault(r => string.Equals(r.Name, current, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && r.Type == "CNAME");
template: var dojoZ = new List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)> {
Dojo.Eq("one CNAME hop", new List<string> { "203.0.113.10" }, Resolve(dojoZ, "WWW.shop.example", "A"));
Dojo.Eq("two hops, two IPs", new List<string> { "198.51.100.7", "198.51.100.8" }, Resolve(dojoZ, "cdn.shop.example", "A"));
hints: Loop: try direct records, else follow the CNAME, else return empty.

steps.title: Migration check
prompt: Before a cut-over you have the old and new zones. Write `List<string> Changed(old, @new, List<string> names)` returning, in input order,
the names whose **resolved A set** (use your `Resolve`, compare as sorted sequences) differs between the zones. Paste `Resolve` in too.
starter: List<string> Changed(List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)> old, List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)> @new, List<string> names)
solution: List<string> Resolve(List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)> zone, string name, string type)

var dojoN = new List<(string Name, string Type, string Value)>(dojoZ.Where(r => r.Name != "shop.example")) { ("shop.example", "A", "192.0.2.50") };
Dojo.Eq("apex and its alias changed", new List<string> { "shop.example", "www.shop.example" }, Changed(dojoZ, dojoN, new List<string> { "shop.example", "www.shop.example", "cdn.shop.example" }));
Dojo.Eq("nothing changed", new List<string>(), Changed(dojoZ, dojoZ, new List<string> { "shop.example" }));
